conviction_note: Since 2 Nov EVGO trades as a merger-arb name. LS Power, which holds 56% of the vote, made a non-binding $2.00 cash proposal, and the stock sits at $1.7825, 10.9% below it. The company has said it will not comment on the process, so the Q3 print is unlikely to settle the deal inside the window, and a deal-pinned price damps the usual earnings reaction. The small negatives on Q3 phasing and a weak peer offset the small positives (EV-parc demand and the slim chance of deal news), so the sum is 0, p_up is 50 and abs_move is about 4% (the pre-deal median was 3.68%, now pinned below an offer cap with fat tails either way).
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $94.1-94.6m, from two agreeing sources: Benzinga consensus $94.1m (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/EVGO/financials) and Fiscal AI $94.62m via Stocktwits (https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/evgo-stock-clocks-best-day-in-two-years-after-controlling-shareholder-takeover-proposal/cNGaOR6R9PM). EarningsWhispers is an outlier at $108.11m (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/EVGO). EPS is disputed: -$0.12 (Fiscal AI), -$0.15 (EarningsWhispers), -$0.19 (Benzinga). Company FY2026 guide: revenue $400-430m, cut on 2026-08-05 from $410-470m; adj. EBITDA $(25)m to $(5)m; 1,350-1,625 new stalls (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821159/000182115926000017/exhibit991evgoearningsrele.htm). H1 revenue was $192.2m, so H2 must be $208-238m.
positioning_check: Short interest (FINRA, via Equibles): 34,447,390 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, days to cover 10.24, up from 31.08m (DTC 7.15) on 09-30 and down from about 41.4m in August (https://equibles.com/stocks/evgo/shortinterest). That is 10.95% of all 314.5m shares outstanding, but LS Power holds about 178.7m Class A and B shares, so it is roughly 25% of the roughly 136m public float. All of this predates the 2 Nov proposal. Volume on 2 Nov was about 72m shares (+46.8%), so much of the short has probably covered since. The 10-30 settlement is not yet published (Equibles models about 33.9m). Options: the chain is unusable, there is no skew number, and the put/call open-interest ratio is 0.15 (baseline). Run-up: +41.5% over 5 days and +46.1% over 20 days, almost all of it the proposal jump from $1.26 to $1.85 on 2 Nov. The price has since eased to $1.7825.

findings.finding: Controlling holder LS Power (about 56% of the vote, about 178.7m shares) proposed on 2026-11-02 to buy every Class A share it does not own at $2.00 cash: a 59% premium to the $1.26 close of 10-30 and 62% to the 30-day VWAP. The board formed a special committee, and EVgo said it 'does not intend to comment further or disclose any developments'. Spot is $1.7825, a 10.9% arb spread. LS Power rules out selling to a third party and will proceed only with the committee's recommendation, so the print is far more likely to be read through the deal than on its own merits. The positive sign is the small chance of process news (advisers hired, a bump, a definitive agreement) inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior deal-pending print. The proposal day itself moved the stock +46.8% ($1.26 to $1.85). Since then it has drifted to $1.7825 (-3.6%) on no company news.
findings.why_not_priced: The proposal is fully priced as a level. What is not priced is any change in the process. If the market expected a definitive agreement or a bump with the Q3 release, the spread to $2.00 would be near zero rather than 10.9%. The company's no-comment line makes news in the window unlikely, which is why the size is small and the band is wide.
findings.independence: The company's own 8-K press release confirms the terms and the committee (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821159/000182115926000027/exhibit991pressrelease2026.htm). Same filing, so not independent.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar of about $94.4m looks slightly rich against the company's own phasing. H1 revenue was $192.2m (charging $117.1m, eXtend $51.2m, AV/ancillary $23.8m). Q2 non-charging revenue was only $21.2m (eXtend $18.0m, -52% y/y). The company said Q1 and Q4 are the strongest non-charging quarters, Q4 2026 the largest revenue quarter, and about 60% of stall builds fall in Q4. With charging at about $66-68m (Q2 $61.4m, +19% y/y), Q3 needs about $27m of non-charging to hit $94m, against $21m in Q2. So a modest headline miss inside an unchanged FY guide is plausible, and a further FY cut is the tail.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): revenue beat ($82.6m vs $79.9m) but FY guide cut, stock -11.56%. Q1 2026 -3.23%, Q4 2025 -5.3%. The guide line has been sold, but those reactions all predate the $2.00 proposal, which now caps and floors the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus did not visibly back-load non-charging revenue into Q4 the way the company described it. If it had, the Q3 bar would sit nearer $88-90m. This is an inference from the company's phasing, not a reported number, it lands inside the FY guide, and the deal pins the price, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Quartr's Q2 call summary: eXtend guide raised to $90-95m, AV/ancillary $40-45m, Q4 the largest quarter, about 60% of stall builds in Q4 (https://quartr.com/events/evgo-inc-evgo-q2-2026_3PfhOtDd). Same company source, different document. AI-generated summary.

findings.finding: Peer Blink Charging reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05, after EVgo last spoke. Revenue was $18.4m against $27.0m a year earlier, charging service revenue fell 11.5% y/y, Q3 revenue missed internal projections and the FY2026 revenue guide was cut to $78-81m from $83-90m. Adj. EBITDA turned positive at $0.2m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured: EVgo's past reactions to peer prints are not in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, but Blink is mostly L2 charging and hardware. Blink's service decline was a deliberate portfolio cut, while EVgo's charging revenue has grown double digits 18 quarters running. A weak proxy, sized small. A move in EVGO on 5-6 Nov would show it was being read across, and the drift was within arb noise.
findings.independence: Proxy. EVgo's own Q2 charging revenue grew +19% y/y, which points the other way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001821159/000182115926000017/exhibit991evgoearningsrele.htm).

findings.finding: Cox Automotive estimates US EV sales in Q3 2026 at 262,649 units, +6.1% q/q and -39.5% y/y against the record Q3 2025. EV share was 6.4%, up from 5.8% in Q2 and the highest since Q3 2025, and Cox cites high gas prices. Charging demand follows the EV parc, which keeps growing, so a sequential rise in throughput (Q2: 99 GWh, +13% y/y) is supported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Charging network revenue has beaten in recent quarters while the stock fell on the non-charging lines and the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed. Throughput lagged stall growth in Q2 (276 kWh/day per public stall vs 281). Small.
findings.independence: Proxy only. EVwire repeats the same Cox data (https://evwire.com/p/tesla-outsells-all-other-ev-brands-combined-us-q3-2026-cox-automotive).

findings.finding: Short interest at the 2026-10-15 settlement was 34.4m shares, DTC 10.2, roughly 25% of the public float outside LS Power's stake. That was set before the $2.00 proposal. Some shorts are probably still covering or recasting as arb hedges, which leans against any sharp post-print selloff while the price stays below $2.00.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The proposal day traded about 72m shares, about 10x the 20-day average, consistent with heavy covering.
findings.why_not_priced: The 10-30 and 11-13 settlements are unpublished, so no one can see how much short remains after the proposal. Zero net, because the deal cap limits any squeeze to the spread.
findings.independence: Massive gives 31.08m and DTC 7.2 for 09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/evgo), the same FINRA series.

findings.finding: Finviz carries a Proactive headline dated 2026-11-04 saying UBS downgraded EVgo to 'neutral', weighing upside against deal risk. That is consistent with sell-side ratings collapsing toward the $2.00 offer. The note itself was not retrieved.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock eased from $1.85 to about $1.78 over 3-6 Nov.
findings.why_not_priced: Already in the price: the downgrade predates the sealed spot. Filed for completeness at 0.
findings.independence: none (headline only, not confirmed by a second source)

outside_window.finding: A definitive merger agreement after the special committee negotiates. Controlling-holder long-form mergers typically take weeks to months to sign, and a committee-negotiated bump above $2.00 is common. That would close the 10.9% spread or more, but it is unlikely to land by 2026-11-10.

rejected_candidates.candidate: EarningsWhispers Q3 revenue estimate of $108.11m as the bar
rejected_candidates.detail: Two other sources agree on about $94.1-94.6m, and the company's guide and phasing (Q4 largest) do not support $108m in Q3. It is kept in `bar` as an outlier rather than used.

rejected_candidates.candidate: CEO RSU grant of 796,813 units at $0 on 2026-09-25 (Form 4)
rejected_candidates.detail: A routine equity grant, not a purchase or sale. It carries no information on the print beyond management's stake in the deal price, which the proposal finding already covers.

baseline_tension: The +41.5% five-day run-up is the takeover proposal, not priced optimism about the quarter. With no usable option chain or skew, the market's only directional statement is the 10.9% discount to a $2.00 cash offer. Nothing found cuts against that: the print should move the stock less than its pre-deal history suggests.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide) and lesson 7 (crowded short against a negative): the Q3 phasing and guide finding went from -0.7 to -0.4. It is an inference that lands inside the FY guide, on a name with about 25% of float short before the deal.

Lesson 3 / two readings of one document: the draft listed the CEO RSU Form 4 as a 0.0 finding. It was moved to rejected_candidates as covered by the deal finding, so the count drops from 7 to 6 and the sum is unchanged.
With the sum now 0.0, p_up went from 48 to 50 and expected_move_pct from -0.16 to 0.0. abs_move_pct is unchanged at 4.0.
Lessons 1, 5 and 8 changed nothing. The Blink and Cox proxies were already small, and coverage is not thin.
